objectives_print: To enable the students to understand about the warping and sizing machines.
To enable the students to understand about the weaving process of power loom, including different shedding mechanisms.
To enable the students to understand detailed concepts related to Dobby and auxiliary motion.
To enable the students to understand detailed concepts related to Jacquard and its recent developments and calculation related to Jacquard.
To enable the students to understand detailed concepts related to multiple box motion and their types and production Technology.

units.1: Objectives of warping, types of warping, material flow in beam warping and sectional warping machines, types of creels used in warping machines. Objectives of sizing, types of sizing machines, principle of two cylinder and multi-cylinder sizing machine, concept of modern sizing machine. Need for drawing-in and denting-in operation, manual and automatic drawing-in and denting-in, leasing, knotting and pinning process in machines.
units.2: General description of plain power looms, Introduction to primary, secondary and auxiliary motion of plain power looms. Tappet shedding, over and under pick motions, Beating-up Mechanism – Eccentricity of sley, Loom timing of Primary motion, Negative and positive take up motion, five wheel and seven wheel take up motion, positive & negative let-off motions.
units.3: Scope & limitation of tappet shedding, Detailed study of various types of tappet shedding mechanism, Scope & limitation of dobby, negative and positive dobby, right hand & left hand dobby & their pegging methods, Brief description of Knowles dobby, cross border dobby, heald reversing motion.
units.4: Types of jacquards and working principles, size and figuring capacity of jacquard, single lift single cylinder Jacquard, Double lift single cylinder, double lift double cylinder, Electronic jacquard, split harness, Different system of harness tie- up. Calculation related to Jacquard, Harness and Design- set of harness, number of harness cords to each hook, casting out and size of repeat.
units.5: Multiple box motion and their types, Pick-at will, pick and pick motion. Detailed study of various motions of automatic looms: pirn change, shuttle change loom, mechanical warp stop motions, electro-mechanical warp stop motion. Warp protective mechanism: loose reed & fast reed, weft detection mechanism side and center weft fork motion. Loom shed calculation-efficiency, production and production planning.

cos.text: To identify the process of warping, sizing, & drawing machines and denting process.
To demonstrate the weaving process of power loom, including different shedding mechanisms.
To summarize the working of different Dobby and auxiliary motion.
To illustrate working principles of Jacquard, its recent developments and calculation.
To describe the different types of multiple box motion and loom shed calculation.

objectives_print: To enable the students to understand the basic concepts about dyes and pigments.
To enable the students to understand the theory of dye bath assistant, chemical auxiliaries and dyeing process parameters.
To enable the students to understand the detailed concept related to dyeing with Acid, Basic, Metal complex dyes on textile fibres.

units.1: Introduction to colouring materials. Definition and classification of colouring materials: Dyes, pigments and lakes. Dye-fibre interactions: physical, chemical, solid-solid and mechanical interactions. Terminologies used in dyeing: Affinity, substantivity, exhaustion, fixation, percentage of shade, expression. Assessment of colour fastness: Colour fastness to washing, light, rubbing & perspiration.
units.2: Dye bath assistant, chemical auxiliaries and process parameters such as temperature, pH, time and material to liquor ratio (M.L.R) in dyeing. Principles, recipe, dyeing mechanism and method of application of Direct, Reactive, Vat, Azoic, a n d Sulphur dyes on cellulosic fibre. Dyeing of regenerated fibres with viscose, model, and lyocel.
units.3: Acid, Basic, Metal complex dyes on textile fibres (Nylon, silk, wool) with effect of process parameters and function of chemicals. Principles, recipe, dyeing mechanism and application of Disperse dyes on Polyester. Various methods of dyeing Polyester such as Carrier, High temperature, High Pressure and thermosol dyeing. Dyeing of blends: Polyester/Cotton, Polyester/Viscose and Polyester/Wool.
units.4: Introduction to Printing. Difference between dyeing and printing. Ingredients in the print paste, Brief introduction to methods of printing: Block and screen printing by hand, semi-automatic and fully automatic flatbed screen printing, rotary screen printing. Styles of printing: Direct, discharge and resist style. Printing process with Direct, Reactive, and Acid dyes. After treatments in printing: Steaming and curing.
units.5: Objective of textile finishing, Classification of finishing processes, Mechanical and chemical finishes. Brief introduction to mechanical finishing: Calendaring and sanforizing. Brief introduction to chemical finishing processes: Crease proofing, softening and stiffening, flame retardant, water proof & water repellent finishing.

cos.text: To describe various aspects of dyes, pigments and various terms related to.
To use dye bath assistant, chemical auxiliaries and dyeing process parameters and mechanism involved in the process.
To apply the knowledge in dyeing methods for different dyes like Acid, Basic, Metal complex dyes on textile fibres.

subjects.name_print: QUALITY EVALUATION OF FIBERS AND YARNS
subjects.scheme_line_print: 3. BHT-503 Quality Evaluation of Fibers and Yarns T PCS 3 1 0 20 10 30 70 100 4
subjects.header_print: BHT 503 QUALITY EVALUATION OF FIBERS AND YARNS 3L:1T:0P 4 Credits
objectives_print: To make the students understand the principle and method of working of equipment’s used for testing of fibres and yarns.
To make the students understand the concepts related to tensile testing modes like CRT, CRE, CRL.
To make the students understand the properties of different fibers& yarn technique.
To make the students understand the concepts related to yarn evenness, twist and yarn strength.
To make the students understand the concepts related to different aspects of yarn testing.

units.1: Scope and Objectives of testing of textile materials; concept of quality; Selection of samples for quality assessment – random and biased samples – squaring technique and zoning technique for fibre selection; yarn sampling - use of random numbers - sampling for various types of yarn tests- yarn strength, linear density, elongation, twist.
units.2: Moisture relation and testing: standard atmosphere condition, moisture regain and moisture content and measurement of atmospheric condition, Fiber testing: Fibre length and length uniformity measuring techniques; Fibre strength and its relation to yarn strength. Fiber bundle strength tests. HVI, AFIS
units.3: Fibre fineness – definition- comparison of various fibres – its importance in yarn manufacture; measurement techniques. Cotton fibre maturity, estimation by microscopic method - maturity ratio and index, estimation by other methods – optical, air flow, differential dyeing; its importance in spinning. Fibre trash – influence on quality; measurement – principle and estimation of micro-dust for rotor spinning. High volume instrument for total fiber quality measurement.
units.4: Yarn Appearance and grading, yarn mass evenness parameters – measurement –nature of irregularity: - index of irregularity; limit irregularity electronic mass evenness determination – Yarn fault classification –Yarn abrasion resistance – importance and measuring technique. Yarn hairiness – importance and assessment techniques. Twist in single and ply yarns –twist direction – twist factor – twist and yarn strength; twist measurement and breaking twist angle measurement. Analysis of data and test reports such as, Classimat.
units.5: Tensile characteristics – Tensile Strength Testing modes – CRT, CRE and CRL, study of strength, single yarn strength; Lea count strength product (CSP) and Corrected Count Strength Product (CCSP), elongation, work of rupture, initial modulus, work factor and yield point – determination of yield point. Stress-strain relations of natural and manmade fibres, influence of fibre structure, humidity and temperature on tensile characteristics. Time effects Study of creep phenomena. Elastic recovery and its relation to stress and strain of fibres; mechanical conditioning of fibres and its influence on elastic recovery. Load cycling and extension cycling-their effect on elastic recovery. Introduction about torsional and flexural rigidity of fibers.

cos.text: To define the scope and objectives of testing of textile materials.
To explain about Moisture relation and testing for textiles.
To describe the testing methods of fibre fineness and maturity.
To explain different yarn grading system and evenness testing.
To describe the tensile behavior of yarns.

objectives_print: To enable the students to learn about the fiber forming process, fiber morphology and its application areas.

To expose the students to advances in the melt spinning process.
To brief students to advances in the solution spinning process.

units.1: Evolution of Manufactured fiber, Fiber forming process, Fiber products and properties, Molecular orientation and crystallinity in fibers, Polymer as Fiber, Plastics and Rubber, Fiber Morphology, Thermal Transitions. Application area.
units.2: Phenomena of fluid flow during fiber spinning: Shear Flow- Viscose flow and Newtonian fluids, capillary flow. Non-Newtonian Fluids - Time-independent fluids & Time-dependent fluids, Factor affecting shear viscosity, Spinnability of fluids, Flow Instabilities – dieswell and melt fracture, draw resonance.
units.3: Melt Spinning: Spinning Line - Feature, extruder, spinning manifold, spin pack & spinneret, cooling system. Melt spinning variables and Conditions for Continuous Spinning, Special Features of High Speed Spinning – LOY, POY, FOY, and HOY. Structure development in Polyester and Nylon during spinning.
units.4: Solution Spinning: Process variable in solution spinning. Dry-Spinning – Preparation of dope, Spinning process – spinning cell, fiber cross-section formation, spin-stretch during dry-spinning, finish application and winding. Wet-Spinning – Solution Preparation and Transport, Coagulation- coagulation process, Spin-stretch during coagulation, structure and morphology of fiber in solution-spinning, Salient features of solution spinning.
units.5: Post-Spinning Operations: Drawing - drawing systems, influence of drawing on structure and properties of fibres, Heat setting- Types of heat setting, influence of heat setting on fiber behavior, Spin finish - Importance of Spin finish composition & application, Texturing- classification & different techniques of texturizing. Introduction and use of high performance fibers- Aramids, Carbon, Glass.

objectives_print: To enable the student to know about process control and quality assessment of Pre-Spinning
To enable the student to know about process control yarn productions.
To enable the student to know about process of winding and warping in weaving Process.
To enable the student to know about process control and quality assessment of Sizing.
To enable the student to know about process control in Textile Chemical Processing.

units.1: Importance of Process control in textiles. Control of mixing quality and cost, determination of trash content and cleaning efficiency of blow room and card , control of neps generation and fibre rupture in blow room and card, yarn quality characteristics affected by blow room and card, neps removal efficiency (NRE) in carding, factor affecting NRE in carding. control of process parameter in blow room and carding.
units.2: Influence of roller setting, construction of top and bottom roller and draft distribution on yarn characteristics, optimum level of comber waste, improvement in mean length in combing, maximizing machine efficiency in ring frame, controlling the end breakage rate in ring frame, control of yarn realization. Control of count variability, unevenness, imperfection and yarn faults.
units.3: Process Control in Winding: characteristics of good splice-appearance and strength rating, yarn faults classification by Classimate, yarn clearer setting adjustment and removal of yarn faults, package defects, Relative humidity and temperature. Process Control in warping: Control of end breaks, tension levels, quality. Process Control in Pirn Winding: Minimising End breaks, stoppages due to mechanical failure.
units.4: Process Control in Sizing: Choice of size recipe and preparation, control of size pick-up, control of yarn stretch in different zones, Control of moisture in sized yarn. Control of Productivity in loom shed, control of loom efficiency and stoppages.
units.5: Process control in textile pre-treatment - Desizing, Scouring, Bleaching, Souring, Mercerizing. Process control in dyeing and printing of textiles- Basic requirements of water quality for dyeing, Influence of Liquor ratio, auxiliaries, temperature, pH in reactive dyeing, Process control in printing paste formulation. Process control in finishing of textiles- Stenter, sanforising, Calendaring process, and Chemical finishes- Softener, Resin, Fire retardants, and water repellent and finish.
